findings.description: The reports_archive bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration block, so stored report objects rely solely on defaults rather than an explicitly enforced (and ideally KMS-backed) encryption configuration. For an archive that may hold sensitive business data, encryption at rest is not asserted in the configuration.

The ledger_exports bucket contains no server_side_encryption_configuration block. Ledger/financial exports are highly sensitive, and there is no explicit enforcement of SSE-KMS encryption at rest for this data.

The model_artifacts bucket enables versioning and logging but defines no server_side_encryption_configuration, so model artifacts are not covered by an explicitly declared encryption-at-rest configuration.

The ops_runbooks bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration block; runbooks frequently contain operational detail (endpoints, procedures, sometimes credentials) and are stored without an explicitly enforced encryption configuration.

The vendor-roster.xlsx object is uploaded with no kms_key_id or server_side_encryption specified, so this potentially sensitive/PII-bearing seed object is stored using only the bucket default rather than an explicitly enforced encryption configuration.
